title: The Hidden Reason You Ignore Facts That Contradict Your Beliefs
hook: We naturally seek information that supports what we already think.

narration.text: We naturally seek information that supports what we already think.
This is called confirmation bias, a common cognitive shortcut.
Our brains prefer information that fits easily with existing mental models.
It takes less effort to process familiar ideas than new ones.
This bias can make it hard to change our minds, even with new evidence.
It shapes how we interpret news, scientific findings, and social interactions.
Recognising it helps us consider different perspectives more openly.
Have you noticed this tendency in yourself or others?

description: Discover why our brains often filter information to confirm what we already believe. This cognitive bias influences how we see the world and process new ideas, making it challenging to shift perspectives. Understanding confirmation bias can help us become more critical thinkers.
topic: Why you often seek out information that confirms your existing beliefs.
